newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bunds stuck sideways, M3 fails to excite.
newsitem.headline: German bunds stuck sideways, M3 fails to excite.

text.p: German Bunds were quoted largely unchanged in late trade on Monday, with the latest German money supply data failing to give any new impulse to the market.
December Bund futures traded at 99.59 at 1513 GMT, around the same as morning levels, with a range seen at 99.50 to 99.70.

News earlier that German M3 money supply growth had fallen to 8.4 percent from 8.7 percent was largely ignored. Dealers said market attention was more focused on U.S. bonds, and there were no major U.S. indicators for them to react to today.
Strong technical resistance is also seen for the contract at 99.70, and higher at 99.83-85. "I don't see a massive rise. We'd have to knock out 99.83-85 first," one dealer said.
The benchmark 10-year 6.25 percent April cash Bund was quoted at 101.86/92, slightly up from Friday's close of 101.83.
October inflation data from the first four German states to report in the next few days were also not expected to have much of an impact on the market.
"Even good figures will not change the rate outlook. The only danger is of an unpleasant surprise," one dealer said.
